title: PCache bulk/static/heap page allocation, free, and status accounting

scope.rationale: These functions initialize per-cache bulk pages, allocate page objects from bulk-local storage or configured process slots before one contiguous Manager fallback, classify static versus heap pressure, update source status slots, and return or release each storage class in source order.

dependencies.caller_closure: Production Cache creation and destruction route through bulk-local, static-slot, and process-Manager heap branches. Direct Lifecycle.pageMalloc/pageFree use the same static and Manager primitives.

inputs: Requested contiguous page/header/extra size, per-cache maximum, signed nInitPage configuration, and initialized process PCache lifecycle
outputs: Eight-byte-aligned static slot when eligible/available, otherwise one rounded contiguous heap allocation, or null/OOM
contracts.ownership: Bulk storage is one Manager allocation owned by Cache and split into cache-local pages returned to its free list; static slots are borrowed from Lifecycle; ordinary heap ownership transfers to Cache. Every class is returned or freed exactly once.
contracts.state_and_results: On an empty cache with nMax>=3, positive nInitPage selects a page count and negative nInitPage selects KiB, capped by nMax. Bulk-local pages precede process slots. Static pop/push updates free count/pressure/PAGECACHE_USED; ordinary fallback updates PAGECACHE_OVERFLOW; successful process allocations update MEMORY_USED. Pressure selects the static-pool flag only when configured slots can fit page-plus-extra; otherwise it selects Manager heap-nearly-full state.
contracts.locks_callbacks_io: STATIC_PMEM serializes global free slots, static pressure, and PCache status. STATIC_MEM serializes Manager allocation and heap-nearly-full state. No I/O; benign bulk allocation has no externally visible callback.
contracts.failure_and_continuation: Bulk allocation is benign: OOM continues into ordinary page allocation. Static exhaustion falls back to Manager heap. Heap/hash OOM restores popped or allocated ownership and later fetch continues.

representation_differences: Source PgHdr1 and higher PgHdr layers are adjacent C records; Zig Page is placed at an aligned offset in the same bulk/static/heap chunk and records its storage class explicitly.
Cache-local free pages use Page.bulk_next instead of PgHdr1.pNext; the single bulk allocation and chunk arithmetic, precedence, cap, and release behavior are preserved.
Lifecycle.pageMalloc/pageFree provide direct utility transport; production Cache uses the same static and Manager-backed primitives.
MEMTYPE_PCACHE debug tags are represented by explicit bulk_local/static_slot/process_heap ownership fields.
Source compares szPage+szExtra before selecting static pressure; Cache passes native page_size+extra_size while its Zig Page metadata remains outside that comparison.

oracle.protocol: The C/Zig PCache differential's first 782 scope observations include two-slot static exhaustion/restoration and static-versus-heap pressure selection, three-page bulk precedence, ordinary overflow, and shrink release. Native tests cover positive page-count mode, negative KiB mode, nMax cap, benign bulk OOM fallback, sticky ordinary OOM, status restoration, and sixteen concurrent direct allocations.
internal_observations: benign bulk OOM then ordinary fallback
soft-create pressure rejection and clean-page recycling
oracle.normalization: Heap/static addresses are allocation identities; counts, ranges, rounded sizes, status values, ownership, results, and event order are exact.

assurance.oom: One-shot bulk OOM is benign and falls through to ordinary Manager allocation; sticky process OOM leaves Memory/PCache status and Cache ownership unchanged; hash rollback is leak-free.
assurance.io_crash_concurrency: No I/O. STATIC_PMEM protects slot pressure and STATIC_MEM protects heap pressure; sixteen-thread allocation restoration passes and exact C/Zig pressure selection is differential-tested.
assurance.malformed_input: Oversized requests bypass static slots; lifecycle manager validates static configuration.
assurance.continuation: Bulk OOM fallback, static return, ordinary OOM, clear/reuse, shrink release, and subsequent fetch are tested.
assurance.performance: Bulk initialization is one allocation plus one linear chunk-link pass; bulk/static pop and push are constant-time; ordinary fallback is one Manager allocation.

integration.production_owner: src/core/page_cache.zig Lifecycle plus Cache contiguous page storage
integration.native_call_path: Pager.open uses Cache.initWithLifecycle(activeProcessLifecycle); first fetch applies signed initial_pages bulk policy before static-slot and ordinary Manager allocation.
integration.bounded_owner_retired: Cache no longer ignores nInitPage, configured slots, process Manager, or source storage precedence, and no longer performs three heap allocations per ordinary page.

independent_review.notes: Requires independent review of chunk layout representation, the explicit PGroup dependency boundary, exact status/ownership traces, and concurrent behavior.

known_blockers: PGroup-wide cross-cache LRU, purgeable counters, and source-shaped hash buckets are integrated in a separate scaffolded unit pending exact object-allocation and upper-cache coupling.

implementation_spans: upstream/sqlite/src/pcache1.c was reviewed completely, with lines 297-526 covering bulk initialization, static-slot/heap allocation and free, page object allocation/free, public page allocation wrappers, and pressure selection
The PgFreeslot, PgHdr1.isBulkLocal, PCache1.pFree/pBulk layouts and their initialization, classification, and teardown sites were reviewed in the same file

src/core/page_cache.zig Lifecycle slot/overflow transport and Cache contiguous bulk/static/heap page owners, nearby Pager-facing cache operations, source-identity comments, and native tests were reviewed; mapped targets are AST-hashed
callers: pcache1FetchStage2 reaches pcache1AllocPage after soft-admission/recycling; remove/truncate/destroy/enforcement reach pcache1FreePage
sqlite3PageMalloc/PageFree expose the same static-slot then heap allocator to other page-oriented internals
Native Pager.open constructs Cache with activeProcessLifecycle; production fetch, discard, truncate, shrink, clear, and deinit exercise all storage classes
callees: InitBulk rejects disabled/small caches, computes count or negative-KiB bytes capped at nMax, performs benign one-allocation acquisition, splits aligned page/header/extra chunks, and publishes a cache-local free chain
pcache1Alloc pops an eligible static slot under STATIC_PMEM and updates pressure/PAGECACHE_USED/SIZE; exhaustion or oversize falls back to sqlite3Malloc and PAGECACHE_OVERFLOW
pcache1Free classifies by configured range, pushes static slots and restores pressure/status, or retags/accounts/frees heap ownership

AllocPage gives bulk-local precedence, brackets optional benign ordinary allocation, builds contiguous pBuf/PgHdr1/pExtra layout, and increments the selected purgeable counter only on success; FreePage reverses owner and counter transitions
UnderMemoryPressure reads static pressure only when configured slots fit page plus extra, otherwise delegates to heap-nearly-full
assertions_branches_cleanup: All 40 behavior IDs cover disabled/capped/count/KiB bulk modes, benign OOM, static eligibility/exhaustion/accounting, heap fallback/accounting, null/range free, bulk precedence, alignment, purgeable counters, and pressure selection
Bulk allocation is one cache owner split into borrowed page chunks and is released only when every chunk has returned; static slots are borrowed process owners; overflow is one Manager heap owner
STATIC_PMEM protects free-chain/count/pressure/status; the selected active profile does not enable memory-management mutex release/reentry branches
Hash insertion OOM rolls newly acquired storage back through its exact class; ordinary sticky OOM leaves counters and owners unchanged
upstream_tests: upstream pcache2.test and memsubsys1.test exercise configured slots, exhaustion, fallback, PAGECACHE_USED/OVERFLOW/SIZE, release, and wrong-size bypass; shrink/cache-size/OOM suites cover lifecycle continuation

Project page-cache tests cover direct and Cache slot use, bulk count/KiB/cap/preference/release, benign bulk OOM, sticky overflow OOM, pressure selection, hash rollback, status restoration, and sixteen concurrent allocations
The PCache differential compares storage identity/class, counters, pressure, LRU interactions, event order, and continuation; PGroup coupling is owned by the dependent dossier
